newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: No deal yet on Pol Pot's exile, Ranariddh says.
newsitem.headline: No deal yet on Pol Pot's exile, Ranariddh says.

text.p: No deal has yet been worked out to send Pol Pot, the murderous Khmer Rouge leader, into exile, Cambodia's Co-Premier Norodom Ranariddh said on Friday.
"No, No, I think we have to wait for some developments," Ranariddh told reporters during an Asia-Pacific conference he is attending in Kuala Lumpur.
"I think the story is not confirmed," he said. "I hope a third country will give asylum to Pol Pot."
Members of Ranariddh's party have said a peace settlement with the Khmer Rouge is imminent and its nominal leader Khieu Samphan would be allowed to enter politics.
Under the purported deal, Pol Pot and two other senior commanders would go into exile and rank-and-file guerrillas would join the government side.
Khieu Samphan is the official leader of a hard-line Khmer Rouge faction still at war with the coalition government, though most political analysts say Pol Pot is the real leader.

The agreement has not been confirmed by the government but military officials and diplomats say negotiations between Ranariddh's party and the Khmer Rouge, allies during the Cambodian war in the 1980s, have been taking place.
In a guerrilla radio broadcast last month, Khieu Samphan said he would support an alliance formed by Ranariddh.
Political analysts say Ranariddh's rival and co-premier, Hun Sen, is keen to prevent any such agreement in the run-up to next year's election.

The Khmer Rouge, responsible for the death of more than one million people during their 1975-1979 "killing fields" rule, has been hard hit by government offensives, defections and splits since boycotting a 1993 election.
But although the rebels have lost military might, they have gained political muscle as the two feuding premiers have vied to win the guerrillas over to their respective ranks.
